A1.justification: Both PDFs present Perspective-Invariant 3D Object Detection, the Pi3DET dataset, and Pi3DET-Net. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, detector comparisons, component ablations, and ROS/jitter analyses in Tables 2–6 and 10–13, with qualitative results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original Pi3DET-Net experiments, detector benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-stage PA/KA procedure, RPJ, VPP, GTD, probabilistic feature alignment, and associated objectives in Section 4 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same Pi3DET platforms, nuScenes and KITTI tasks, annotation-pretraining sources, and six cross-platform plus two cross-dataset settings. STF disappears only from the related-dataset overview, not from evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 6 omits SECOND-IOU, PillarNet, and PV-RCNN-C from the reported IoU 0.7 comparison, reducing its baseline detector set from 18 to 15. These methods remain in Appendix Table 13 at IoU 0.5; the other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, backbones, 20/40-epoch training budgets, augmentations, confidence threshold, and AP evaluation protocols remain unchanged in Section 5.1 and Appendices B and C.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 5, ROS analysis in Table 10 and Figure 8, jitter sensitivity in Table 11, and qualitative/failure analyses in Appendix C are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report AP point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing descriptive distribution statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: Three result rows disappear from Table 6, including average BEV/3D AP@0.7 values of 48.42/30.40 for SECOND-IOU, 43.97/24.69 for PillarNet, and 48.62/37.02 for PV-RCNN-C. Retained numerical results and qualitative findings match; no new performance gains are reported.

T1.justification: The geometric definitions, transformation equations, Gaussian/KL formulation, and loss objectives are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset, adaptation-framework, and benchmark contributions, including the same novelty and generalization claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretations of ROS instability and platform-dependent jitter, alongside limitations involving extreme viewpoints, distant sparse targets, base-detector dependence, and predefined sensing ranges.

D1.justification: The front-page GitHub link target changes from pi3det/toolkit to worldbench/pi3det, revising the documented code-access location. Implementation settings, hardware, dataset access, and licensing details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Table 1 removes STF from the comparison with prior datasets, although its paper remains cited elsewhere. The related-work narrative and matched set of 122 references otherwise remain stable; renumbering and bibliographic updates do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: Limited wording, appendix-pointer, and bibliographic edits accompany replacement of institutional affiliations with WorldBench Team and removal of the Acknowledgments. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column format with a mostly single-column design, redesigns the title/abstract block, and extensively resizes and relocates tables and appendix figures. Table structures and captions also receive edits, while the underlying scientific figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Larger tables improve legibility, but v2 removes three detectors' IoU 0.7 results from Table 6 without preserving them elsewhere. Their retained IoU 0.5 results in Table 13 do not replace that stricter comparison. This modest loss of benchmark completeness outweighs the presentation benefits; the method, central results, and supporting analyses otherwise remain unchanged.
